FINDINGS simplicity PR#12185 @b6002f6b6c69370f8c18a9e6c1cafa8463273a6b
- path: model/model.go
  line: 285
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P3
  confidence: 0.98
  reachability: plausible
  claim: A nil Positions tensor now panics before the existing invalid-batch error can be returned.
  evidence: model/model.go:285 calls `batch.Positions.Dim(0)` unconditionally; the merge-base used `len(batch.Positions)`, so a zero-value `input.Batch` reached the explicit “batch size cannot be less than 1” error instead of dereferencing nil.
  fix: Check `batch.Positions == nil` before calling `Dim`.
- path: kvcache/wrapper.go
  line: 50
  side: RIGHT
  severity: nit
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: plausible
  claim: The unwind path rematerializes the identical positions slice once for every cache being unwound.
  evidence: kvcache/wrapper.go:49-52 places `batch.Positions.Ints()` inside the `j` loop; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1029-1037 shows that `Ints()` may synchronize and allocate.
  request: Move `curPositions := batch.Positions.Ints()` before the unwind loop.
  fix: Read the positions once per failed `StartForward` call and reuse them for every prior cache.

FINDINGS baseline PR#12185 @b6002f6b6c69370f8c18a9e6c1cafa8463273a6b
- path: kvcache/causal.go
  line: 203
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P1
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: routine
  claim: Cache reservation must derive batch size without reading tensor storage, because no-allocation model-fit requests provide tensors with no backing data.
  detail: `LoadOperationFit` disables allocation, so the newly created positions tensor has a nil data pointer and `Ints()` returns nil; `StartForward` consequently records a zero batch size, and the first cache `Put` panics when the model produces a nonzero batch, causing routine memory-fit requests for cached models to fail.
  evidence: runner/ollamarunner/runner.go:1203-1205 selects `AllocMemory: false` for fit; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:926-935 does not populate `FromIntSlice` storage in that mode; ml/backend/ggml/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:38-51 creates a no-allocation buffer with a null base; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1029-1040 therefore returns nil from `Ints`; kvcache/causal.go:203-204 derives `curBatchSize` as zero, while kvcache/causal.go:584-591 compares it with the model tensor's actual batch dimension and panics.
  fix: Derive the reserve-path batch size from tensor shape and avoid reading position values when reservation does not require them.
- path: ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go
  line: 1007
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P2
  confidence: 0.96
  reachability: plausible
  claim: `Bytes` must not treat allocated destination storage as computed output, because doing so makes `ml.Dump` skip pending graph operations and return stale data.
  detail: The new CPU-memory fallback returns bytes whenever `ggml_get_data` is nonnil, but graph operations such as `Copy` are views over a preallocated destination and have nonnil storage before execution; `ml.dump` interprets nonnil `Bytes()` as proof that computation is complete, so dumping converted F16 or quantized tensors reads the untouched destination instead of evaluating the copy.
  evidence: ml/backend.go:551-555 creates an allocated F32 destination and assigns the pending `Copy` result; ml/backend.go:566-573 computes only when `Bytes()` is nil; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1001-1010 now returns the destination bytes before computation; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1280-1284 uses `ggml_cpy`, and ml/backend/ggml/ggml/src/ggml.c:3245-3263 shows that operation is a view of the destination carrying a pending `GGML_OP_CPY`.
  fix: Expose CPU storage directly only for tensors known to contain initialized input data, while preserving nil-before-compute semantics for pending graph results.

FINDINGS validation PR#12185 @b6002f6
- path: ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go
  line: 1007
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P2
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: plausible
  kind: correctness
  tag: "[question]"
  title: CPU Bytes fallback mistakes pending graph output for computed data
  claim: `Bytes` now exposes allocated CPU storage for pending operations, causing `ml.Dump` to skip required computation and decode uninitialized or stale data.
  detail: `ml.Dump` for F16/quantized creates an allocated F32 destination and `t.Copy` returns a pending `ggml_cpy` view over that destination. `dump` checks `Bytes()==nil` to decide whether to execute; now nonnil destination storage makes it skip computation and decode untouched/stale bytes.
  evidence: ml/backend.go:551-568 creates the copy and computes only when `Bytes` is nil; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1001-1010 now returns any nonnil CPU data; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1280-1284 creates the pending copy; ml/backend/ggml/ggml/src/ggml.c:3245-3263 confirms `ggml_cpy` is a graph operation represented as a view of the already-allocated destination.
  fix: Distinguish materialized CPU tensors from pending graph-operation views before using storage presence as the readiness test.
- path: model/model.go
  line: 285
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P3
  confidence: 0.98
  reachability: plausible
  kind: robustness
  tag: "[question]"
  title: Preserve the invalid-batch error for nil Positions
  claim: A zero-value or otherwise malformed `input.Batch` now panics through a nil `Positions` interface instead of returning the prior batch-size validation error.
  detail: `batch.Positions.Dim(0)` dereferences nil, whereas `len` on the former nil slice reached the explicit “batch size cannot be less than 1” error.
  evidence: model/model.go:284-290 invokes `Dim` before any nil guard; model/input/input.go:53-59 declares `Positions` as an `ml.Tensor` interface.
  fix: Check `batch.Positions == nil` before calling `Dim`.

KILLED
- pass-baseline kvcache/causal.go:203 — refuted: no-allocation buffers deliberately receive a nonnil aligned placeholder pointer at ml/backend/ggml/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:127-137, so `Ints` preserves the tensor length; reserve-mode `buildMask` does not read position values at kvcache/causal.go:347-356, and `Put` only compares that length at kvcache/causal.go:584-592.
- pass-simplicity kvcache/wrapper.go:50 — below-bar: this runs only while unwinding an already-failed cache start, and production positions are unsynchronized input tensors from runner/ollamarunner/runner.go:582, for which ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1035-1037 returns a zero-copy slice rather than synchronizing or allocating.

FINDINGS validation PR#12185 @b6002f6b6c69370f8c18a9e6c1cafa8463273a6b
- path: model/models/llama4/model_text.go
  line: 222
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P1
  confidence: 0.97
  reachability: routine
  kind: correctness
  claim: Llama 4’s default attention-temperature path dereferences an unallocated positions tensor during the mandatory Fit pass, causing model initialization to fail before memory requirements can be returned.
  detail: LoadOperationFit sets AllocMemory=false, then reserveWorstCaseGraph wraps batchPositions with FromIntSlice and calls Model.Forward. In this mode FromIntSlice deliberately skips copying the values, while the tensor’s data pointer is only the backend’s small aligned placeholder address. Ints constructs a full-length unsafe slice over that address, and this loop reads every element to calculate attention scales. The same invalid read occurs at kvcache/encoder.go:94 for multimodal reserve batches. CPU-side graph construction must retain real position values rather than dereference no-allocation tensor storage.
  evidence: llm/server.go:709 runs Fit before allocation; runner/ollamarunner/runner.go:1204 disables allocation and runner/ollamarunner/runner.go:1069-1080 creates the positions tensor then forwards it; ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:926-935 skips the copy, ml/backend/ggml/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:127-136 supplies only an aligned placeholder pointer, and ml/backend/ggml/ggml.go:1029-1038 exposes it through unsafe.Slice; model/models/llama4/model_text.go:204 defaults temperature tuning to true and lines 220-223 dereference the slice.
  fix: Preserve host position values for CPU-side calculations during Fit, and do not expose no-allocation placeholder storage through Ints.
